notes:
The whole list is on n92.jpg (printed p. 85). n90 and n91 are the end of the report text, signed by Alexander G. More and Richard M. Barrington. n93 (p. 86) starts the 'General Remarks of Light-Keepers'. The title is 'List of Light-stations.' and the legend is printed below the table: 'o = No reply.  x = Schedule returned partly or wholly filled.  * = No schedule sent to this station.'

Row count: 40 rows are printed, not 42. The OCR did not drop anything. The print itself skips nos. 9 and 35: the numbers run 1–8, 5.*, 8.*, 10–34, 36–40. So there is no Wicklow Head (9) and no Loop Head (35) in this year's list. Treat them as gaps in the numbering, not missing rows.

Columns: Spring and Autumn are headed vertically. Then 'Miles from shore.', then 'Names of Observers.' (no 'Names of Keepers' heading).

How I filled the fields:
- marks: the Spring and Autumn marks, in that order (e.g. 'o x'). None of the station names carries a †, an italic name or any other mark.
- other: the 'Miles from shore' figure, or the printed dash '–' where there is none.
- number: written '5*' and '8*', but printed '5.*' and '8.*'. These are stations inserted after 5 and 8. That asterisk is part of the number and is not the '* = No schedule sent' mark.
- printed: the dot leaders are shortened. Where two observers are printed one above the other with a brace, I wrote it as '{Name and Name.'. The braced rows are 2, 10, 14, 21, 23 and 27.
- keepers: each braced pair is split into two people. I dropped the full stop that ends each row, but kept the full stops in abbreviations (Wm., Robt., W. H., G. H.).
- coast: 'Irish Coast', from the section's running head. There are no sub-headings.
- type: given only for light-ships, printed 'Lt.-ship'. The OCR's 'Lt-ship' at no. 10 is wrong. There is no comma or space in 'Arklow Sth. Lt.-ship,Wicklow'. 'do.' (ditto) under Wexford for nos. 6–7 and under Wicklow for 8.* is kept as printed.

Where the OCR is wrong and the image is clear:
- No. 2 Galley Head is 'x x' (the OCR has 'x *').
- No. 13 is 'Copeland Island, Down x x 3 John Walsh.'
- No. 23 is 'x x 1'.
- Nos. 30 and 31 have 3 miles (the OCR has 8 and §).
- Nos. 36 Samphire Island and 40 Dursey Island have ½ mile.
- Nos. 38 and 39 are 'Valentia, Kerry' and 'Skelligs, Kerry'.
In this type face a 3 looks a little like an 8, but 13, 30 and 31 read as 3.

Spellings copied as printed (don't correct them in the data): 'Howth Baily' (usually Bailey), 'Innishtrahull', 'Arranmore', 'Arran Island' (Aran), 'Rathlin O'Birne', 'Coningbeg', 'Barrels Rock', 'Sth.'. 'Michael Cunniam' is printed so, possibly a misprint of Cunningham. 'John Pinston' and 'Thomas Kerley' are also as printed.

Stations with no observer named: 4 Mine Head, 11 Howth Baily, 31 Slyne Head S., 36 Samphire Island.

Names on more than one station: Patrick Keenan (14 Maidens and 24 Broadhaven), Joseph Hill (21 and 23), John Young (23 and 27). The Redmonds are different people: Henry at 18, John at 27, Robt. W. at 28. Each may be one keeper moved during the year, or different men with the same name.

The General Remarks on n93 confirm 'John Whelan' (spring) and 'John Kelly' (autumn, 'I arrived at this station Nov. 6th') for Galley Head. So a braced pair can mean one keeper replacing another, not two serving together.
